summary.name: Cel-Shaded 3D (Digital and 3D Aesthetics category). The source explicitly names this visual direction. Its status as a style-compatible suggestion is noted where relevant.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: discrete shadow bands, consistent outlines, and selective highlights give 3D forms a drawn appearance. Light direction and outline width stay stable through motion. Realistic gradients and reflections are avoided because they undermine flat shading. The source states this method is distinct from traditional cel production.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: characters and objects where stable shadow bands and outlines are enough. Inferred: stylized explainers, character introductions, and product shots. Inferred: a comic-panel hybrid suits action or promo content when print-like tone should extend the drawn look.
summary.limitations: Explicit: realistic gradients and reflections are excluded. Light direction and outline width must stay fixed. Stepped shading and a deliberate outline method are required. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Palette and renderer limits are unspecified beyond the listed constraints.
summary.palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F4ECD9 (layout), foreground #26394A (layout), accent_1 #547E8F and accent_2 #BA7461 (decorative fills). Gradients are disabled. Shadow bands must be explicitly selected discrete tones from the approved material palette. Task-provided exact colors override these. Foreground on background measures 10.103:1. Accents fail 4.5:1 for body text.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: movement should be smooth and coherent where the action benefits, while deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds stay sharp. Video state derives from composition time. Live pointer or scroll input belongs only to interactive delivery. Reference motions (gaze tracking, orbits, dolly, chaptered transitions) are optional and need suitable eye layers, full 3D geometry, or turntable views.
summary.audio: Unspecified in the source as a fixed requirement; no genre, tempo, instrument, or mandatory layer is assigned. Audio direction is task-specific and optional: music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence. Explicit user audio requirements take precedence. No authorized audio assets are supplied, and speech must remain intelligible and synchronized with picture.
summary.assetRequirements: Explicit: models and textures must be authorized; an exporter string does not establish licensing. glTF assets require inspected node names, materials, pivots, and embedded clips, since clip existence cannot be inferred from filenames. Meshopt decoding applies only when an asset requires it. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Character motion requires eye layers or a rig.
summary.combinations: Suggested: style-031 for comic panels, speed lines, and SFX lettering, keeping outline weight and ink tokens matched. Suggested: style-050 for luminance halftone limited to designated mid-tone bands. Avoid halftone over small faces and unreadable SFX placement. Cel-Shaded 3D alone suits characters where bands and outlines suffice.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit: Three.js with MeshToonMaterial or a stepped toon ramp is the style renderer. Outlines should use depth-normal edges or a dedicated outline renderer, not backface scaling. HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline; Remotion is a fallback only when a limitation is verified and recorded. Libraries: chroma.js validates colors; GSAP provides seekable timelines. Verify decoded frames, seeks, and audio sync.
